subsystems.name: Graphene filler
subsystems.role: provides nanoscale reinforcement or added functionality such as electrical or thermal conductivity.

subsystems.name: Matrix material
subsystems.role: the bulk material that carries load, defines shape and protects the graphene.

subsystems.name: Interface and dispersion system
subsystems.role: ensures the graphene is evenly spread and chemically bonded to the matrix.

subsystems.name: Processing equipment
subsystems.role: shapes the composite into usable parts.

subsystems.name: Characterisation and quality control
subsystems.role: verifies dispersion, bonding and final properties.

buildSteps.title: Produce graphene
buildSteps.detail: Make graphene by liquid-phase exfoliation of graphite, chemical reduction of graphene oxide, or chemical vapour deposition on metal foils. The method sets flake size, defect level and cost.

buildSteps.title: Functionalise the surface
buildSteps.detail: Attach chemical groups such as hydroxyl, carboxyl or amine to the graphene to improve compatibility with the chosen matrix and stop flakes clumping together.

buildSteps.title: Disperse the graphene
buildSteps.detail: Use sonication, high-shear mixing or ball milling in a liquid to separate flakes and form a uniform suspension without breaking them.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with the matrix
buildSteps.detail: Mix the graphene suspension with polymer precursors for in-situ polymerisation, melt-blend with thermoplastics, or stir into molten metal.

buildSteps.title: Shape and cure
buildSteps.detail: Cast, mould, extrude or 3D-print the mixture, then cure or solidify under controlled temperature and pressure.

buildSteps.title: Consolidate and post-process
buildSteps.detail: For metals, sinter or hot-press. For polymers, anneal to improve crystallinity and bonding at the interface.

buildSteps.title: Test and qualify
buildSteps.detail: Measure tensile strength, electrical and thermal conductivity, and use microscopy to check dispersion. Iterate the formulation until properties meet the target.

prerequisites.why: bulk graphene is produced commercially, but single-layer, defect-free flakes remain costly and inconsistent.
preventing clumping and achieving strong bonding between graphene and matrix is still a major research challenge.
existing polymer and metal processing lines can often be adapted for graphene additives.
no universal standards for graphene content, dispersion or toxicity slow commercial adoption.

pathway.milestone: graphene-enhanced sports equipment, coatings and some battery electrodes are on sale
pathway.unlocks: proof of concept and early revenue, but at low volumes.

pathway.milestone: automotive and aerospace parts use graphene at a few percent loading to cut weight or improve strength
pathway.unlocks: larger manufacturing volumes and reliable design data.

pathway.milestone: flexible electronics, printed sensors and biomedical scaffolds use graphene composites
widespread use in structural composites, possibly replacing some carbon-fibre applications
pathway.unlocks: lighter vehicles and aircraft, and new energy storage materials.
